rationale:
Splits the widget bridge's kJSPreamble into two adjacent string literals joined at the call site. No behaviour changes: the joined text is proved byte-identical to the original apart from one blank line at the seam, and adjacent string-literal concatenation happens in translation phase 6, so the compiled program is unchanged.

The change exists because MSVC caps a single string literal at 16380 bytes and the preamble reached 16803 -- 423 over -- when the context-menu branches landed. Only the ARM64 cross-compiler enforces the cap: in one release run windows-x64 compiled the identical file with zero C2026 while windows-arm64 reported one, and clang, GCC and the required macos gate all accepted it. windows-arm64 passed on the three prior releases and failed only on the first containing the context-menu work, so the attribution is measured rather than inferred.

Because that leg gates publication, a tag was cut that shipped no assets. The change therefore also adds an msvc-string-literal-guard ctest, confirmed by control to exit 1 on the pre-fix file and 0 on the fixed one, so the limit now fails on every platform instead of only on the one leg that blocks a release.

No capability family gains, loses or moves authority. The touched file is in render-assets-and-backends only because the bridge preamble lives there; nothing about what the bridge exposes changes.
